answer: The summit multiplier is published, charged in sparrow, and jade lists each payment. The admission burn is multiplied by 13 for each identity already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival pays the most. A burst of registrations hence prices itself out, because the marginal alias burns more than the first by design. A farm of 3549 identities would post 3845 proofs and burn roughly 89 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
